title: Deployment resonance playbook & pin experiments
content:
Purpose:
- Quick personal lab notes for a different kind of canary: 'resonance' = staggered pin + warmup + oscillation checks so we avoid false-positive stability because of cold-cache artifacts.

High-level idea:
- Instead of single-point canary or simple traffic % ramps, we open a small cohort with pinned model version and run a short oscillation: small warmup -> brief backoff -> reapply ramp to test re-priming. Repeat across 3 tenant cohorts to surface cache/priming-sensitive regressions.
- Combine with targeted KV prefill for top client prefixes (sdk + top-10 prefixes) to reduce cold-start noise.

Key heuristics / signals to watch (initial):
- Latency: p50, p95, p99 (token-time and request-time); look for step-changes after reapply.
- Error classes: 5xx, model-timeouts, OOM falls back. Tag by region and hw-type.
- Output quality: run 200-item eval-set for hallucination delta and BLEU-ish/embedding-sim thresholds.
- Cost telemetry: tokens-per-request, average batch size, KV cache hit ratio.
- Behavioral anomalies: increased fallback rate to older model variants, increased client retries.

Cohort plan (sketch):
- Cohort A (pilot): 0.5% traffic, 12h warmup with KV prefill, then 3h backoff to 0.1%, then ramp to 2% over 6h.
- Cohort B (regional probe): 0.2% per region (us-west, eu-central), parallel; same warmup cycle but different peak times.
- Cohort C (heavy-usage anchor): single tenant (~5% traffic for that tenant), run short intense burst to test throughput and burst autoscale.

Pinning lattice notes:
- Pin semantics: service-level model pin override that is sticky per-tenant for 24h unless explicitly unpinned. That's useful to keep cohort stable across oscillations.
- Need a way to expire pins automatically if we detect poor signals (auto-pinback).
- PR: infra/pull/1287 adds pin API endpoints; test harness must exercise TTL expiration.

KV prefill strategy:
- Precompute top prefixes from last 7 days for target tenants (top 10 each). Push KV cache entries to serving nodes immediately prior to warmup.
- Prefill size heuristic: sum(token_count(prefixes)) < 10M tokens per node. If above, fall back to top-3 prefixes only.
- Observability: expose "prefill_hit_ratio" and time-to-first-prefill-hit.

Runbook (quick checklist):
- Preflight (T-minus 48h):
  - [ ] Confirm infra PR merged and canary route config present (see linked PR).
  - [ ] Eval set baseline snapshot (save embeddings + generation samples).
  - [ ] Identify 3 tenants and notify CS owners (ping slack thread).
  - [ ] Schedule quiet window and pager rotation.
- T-minus 1h:
  - [ ] Trigger KV prefill job for cohorts A/B/C.
  - [ ] Stage canary routing rules (no traffic yet).
  - [ ] Health check smoke: dry-run requests against pinned model (5 requests per region).
- Launch (warmup):
  - [ ] Move Cohort A to 0.5% -> monitor first 30m closely (p50/p95).
  - [ ] Validate eval-set runs every 30m; compare to baseline.
- Oscillation phase:
  - [ ] Backoff to 0.1% for 3h -> verify metrics relax to baseline (or record divergence).
  - [ ] Re-ramp to 2% over 6h, re-evaluate cost/quality metrics.
- Decision gates (examples):
  - Severe regression -> immediate rollback (pin back to previous model variant and open rollback incident).
  - Gradual minor regression in p95 latency only -> extend warmup and repeat oscillation once.
  - Quality regression (embedding sim delta > 0.08 on eval set) -> stop and escalate to applied-ml.

Hypotheses we want to test:
- H1: Some regressions only manifest after cache-reprime events; single continuous ramps mask them.
- H2: Prefill reduces transient error-rate spikes by >50% in first 30m.
- H3: Tenant-specific prefix distributions heavily shape warmup length needed.

Open questions / unknowns (TODOs):
- How to surface cache-priming heatmaps in Console (Samir to prototype).
- What bounds for auto-unpin TTL make sense for enterprise customers? (policy discussion with product).
- Do we need a special light-weight eval-set for warmup windows (fast, fewer items) vs full nightly eval?

Notes for next iteration:
- Add a synthetic traffic generator that mimics top-10 prefixes per tenant for more repeatable warmups.
- Try different oscillation patterns: short burst (15m) vs long (3h) to map sensitivity.
- If a cohort triggers fallback, capture full request logs for 30m and mark sample IDs for applied-ml triage.

Quick links / references (local):
- GH PR: infra/pull/1287 -> pin API + route flags
- JIRA: INF-4321 -> "resonance canary experiment"
- Slack: #deployments thread (see linked_artifacts)

Personal quick checklist before I hand off to Lina:
- [ ] Add synthetic prefix generator to repo (small harness).
- [ ] Draft short confluence page with one-slide summary for CS owners.
- [ ] Run one dry oscillation in staging with Cohort A config.

End notes (brain-dump):
- "Resonance" naming helps frame that we're intentionally perturbing the system to find hidden instabilities.
- Keep window sizes conservative for first runs (shorter than we think we need) so we can iterate fast.
- Be explicit about what counts as "primed" vs "stable".

-- Anika
